title: Ward Voice: ranked-choice community polls for council agenda items
context: OurTown is a nonprofit civic-engagement web app (Django + Postgres, self-hosted on the org's existing servers) used by ~18,000 residents of a mid-size US city to follow city council agendas. Mission: increase residents' meaningful participation in local government. Agreed constraint: the product is anonymous-first — residents can participate without verifying identity, and verification is always optional. This plan is about to be dispatched to a 3-person team for a 5-week build.
artifact:
# Ward Voice — build plan

Team: 2 backend, 1 frontend | Duration: 5 weeks | Target launch: before the FY27 budget hearings

## 1. Background
Q3 resident survey (n = 1,240, in-app + library kiosks). "What would make OurTown more useful to you?" (multi-select):
- See how my council member voted on each item, and their stated reason — 61%
- Get notified before items that affect my street or neighborhood — 44%
- Plain-language summaries of agenda items — 37%
- Polls on upcoming items — 9%
Council staff have also told us they lack a structured way to hear from residents between public-comment sessions.

## 2. What we're building
Ward Voice lets staff attach a ranked-choice poll to any agenda item (e.g. "Rank these 5 options for the Elm St. corridor"). Residents rank options; results are shown per ward with instant-runoff tallies. Ward Voice gives residents a direct voice on the items council is actually deciding, and is the centerpiece of the FY27 roadmap.

## 3. Data model
- polls(id, agenda_item_id, options jsonb, opens_at, closes_at)
- poll_responses(id, poll_id, resident_id null, ranking jsonb, ward, verified bool, created_at)
- residents: unchanged. Verified residents already have address, zip, birth_year, gender (collected at optional verification for the jury-pool-style demographic balance reports).
Unverified responses are accepted; ward is self-selected for unverified users and derived from address for verified users.

## 4. Results and open data
- Live results page: instant-runoff rounds, split into "verified" and "all responses" columns.
- Open-data export (weekly, public, CC-BY): one CSV per poll on data.ourtown.org with columns ward, zip, birth_year, gender, ranking, verified, created_at. resident_id is removed before export.
- Council staff get the same CSV plus a PDF summary emailed Monday 07:00.

## 5. Abuse and integrity
- Rate limit: 1 response per poll per device fingerprint + 1 per verified resident; unverified responses over 3/min from one IP are queued for review.
- Results always show verified and unverified tallies separately, so a brigade of unverified responses cannot masquerade as verified sentiment.
- Staff cannot edit or delete responses; poll options are frozen once the first response arrives.

## 6. Outreach (launch week)
To reach residents beyond our current user base:
- Purchase the county voter registration file from the County Clerk ($400, includes mobile numbers where provided).
- Load numbers into Twilio and send an automated SMS to every registered voter in the city (~142,000) with a link to the first poll, then 3 automated reminders over 10 days.
- Reply STOP handled by Twilio's default opt-out.

## 7. Timeline
- Week 1: data model, poll authoring UI for staff.
- Week 2: resident ranking UI (mobile-first, drag or tap-to-rank).
- Week 3: IRV tally, results page, abuse controls.
- Week 4: open-data export, staff PDF, voter-file import + SMS pipeline.
- Week 5: accessibility pass, load test (target 5k concurrent), launch.

## 8. Success metrics
- 6,000 poll responses in the first 30 days.
- 30% of responses from residents not previously active on OurTown.

defects.description: Cross-reference §1 vs §2: residents' top asks are council vote records (61%) and street-level notifications (44%); polls are the lowest-ranked request at 9%. The 5-week build targets the least-wanted feature, and the success metrics measure response volume rather than the participation value the mission names.

The public weekly CSV ties each ranking to ward + zip + birth_year + gender, a quasi-identifier combination that re-identifies many verified residents; removing resident_id is not anonymization. This publishes individuals' positions on contested local items and violates the anonymous-first constraint.
defects.evidence: one CSV per poll on data.ourtown.org with columns ward, zip, birth_year, gender, ranking, verified, created_at

defects.description: Automated mass SMS to ~142,000 purchased voter-file numbers with no prior consent risks TCPA liability for autodialed texts, and voter registration files are commonly restricted by state law to election/political uses — Twilio's STOP handling does not cure either. Needs legal review and a consent-based outreach channel.
defects.evidence: send an automated SMS to every registered voter in the city (~142,000)

decoys: Poll brigading / ballot stuffing by unverified users: handled in §5 by rate limits, review queue, and always-separate verified vs unverified tallies.
Staff tampering with results: handled in §5 — responses are immutable to staff and options freeze after the first response.
